question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (ii).
solution:
The correct answer is '**news**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes the immediate dissemination of information through TVs and radios.
 
• The appropriate noun should indicate something that can be broadcasted or reported immediately.
 
• "**News**" fits well as it conveys the appropriate context of information being shared widely via media channels.
 
• Other options ("**arrow**", "**sceptre**", "**ball**") do not appropriately capture the concept of information dissemination.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *On the afternoon of 30 March 1981, many Americans experienced a 1. feeling__ of déjà-vu. Déjà-vu is a name given to the feeling that a person has seen or experienced an event before. Many Americans could not help having that feeling on this day. The 2. __news__ hit TVs and radios immediately. President Ronald Raegan had been shot. He was leaving a hotel in Washington DC, turned to wave at some of the people gathered to see him, and fell towards the ground. Before he could hit the ground, his Secret Service Agents 3. **________ **him into the car and rushed to the nearest hospital. This same story had been heard before. On 22 November 1963 President John F Kennedy was riding in a motorcade through Dallas, Texas. He smiled and waved to the crowd that had gathered to see him. 4. **________** rang out from a nearby building. The President collapsed into the backseat of the car and was immediately taken to the nearest hospital. He was 5. **________ **dead at the hospital. Now, just seventeen years later, the news sounded eerily the same.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Arrow** (तीर): "Arrow" refers to a weapon or direction indicator and does not suit the context of broadcasting information.
 
• **Sceptre** (राजदंड): "Sceptre" is a ceremonial staff, symbolizing authority, which is unrelated to news dissemination.
 
• **Ball** (गेंद): "Ball" refers to a spherical object, which is inappropriate in the context of information being reported.
